gaps: The executor setting is independent of FORGE_COORDINATOR, but the plan does not route Claude execution when Codex coordinates or Codex execution when Claude coordinates in codex mode. Its verification labels codex mode as native Codex, leaving those combinations unproved (docs/decisions/0085-executor-modes.md:20; plans/active/FORGE-WARM-1-hybrid-mode-reuses-warm-codex-worker-threads.md:238).

Recording Claude sessions in a writer list does not identify what replaces the existing successful-launch requirement at both task-close preflight and stage finish. Claude-only work would still be refused without a plugin launch or degraded window (factory/scripts/forge_cli/stages.py:1831; factory/scripts/forge_cli/stages.py:4362).

The plan pins an external codex binary but specifies only SDK installation through doctor --fix. Today's repair installs @openai/codex@latest, so the proposed exact-version check has no stated way to install or repair its required binary (factory/scripts/forge_cli/doctor.py:1825; factory/scripts/forge_cli/doctor.py:1841).

The supervisor's owner-only socket and 0600 token specify POSIX permissions without a Windows ownership and ACL rule, despite native Windows parity being required. Existing private-file handling uses a separate Windows DACL check for this boundary (plans/active/FORGE-WARM-1-hybrid-mode-reuses-warm-codex-worker-threads.md:173; factory/scripts/forge_cli/delegate.py:1312).

Route stickiness begins at a task's first new-route delegation, but an in-flight pre-upgrade plugin task has no route field to consult. The plan does not say how its existing companion launch rows are recognized before choosing the SDK route (plans/active/FORGE-WARM-1-hybrid-mode-reuses-warm-codex-worker-threads.md:170; factory/scripts/forge_cli/delegate.py:784; docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:81).

An unknown turn blocks close until thread/read reports a terminal state, but the plan gives no recovery when the app-server dies before publishing one or the thread can no longer be read. That leaves a task permanently unable to close despite the repository's bounded-recovery requirement (plans/active/FORGE-WARM-1-hybrid-mode-reuses-warm-codex-worker-threads.md:193; docs/QUALITY.md:121).

Signal resolution currently becomes resolved immediately, with no task-turn identity or delivery acknowledgement. The plan does not define when a resolution counts as delivered, or how existing plugin and historical signals without turn IDs remain valid after the proposed schema change (factory/scripts/forge_cli/signal.py:219; factory/scripts/forge_cli/signal.py:231; factory/schemas/signal.json:6).

The task order enables SDK route selection in SDK-SETUP before the supervisor and admission route exist, then promises a first real SDK delegation and close parity in SDK-ADMISSION before LIVE-EVENTS supplies turn-state reconciliation. The plan needs a safe activation boundary and terminal-state proof for each independently shipped task (plans/active/FORGE-WARM-1-hybrid-mode-reuses-warm-codex-worker-threads.md:220; plans/active/FORGE-WARM-1-hybrid-mode-reuses-warm-codex-worker-threads.md:224).

The proposed end-to-end fixture starts with forge init on the current template. It does not exercise upgrade of an older existing client, preservation of an active plugin task, or a repeated upgrade, which are explicit acceptance outcomes (plans/active/FORGE-WARM-1-hybrid-mode-reuses-warm-codex-worker-threads.md:240; docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:113).

The verification plan names mode and route cells but does not assign falsifiable checks for the confirmed matrix's setup, init/adopt/upgrade, scoped writes, hook delivery, and task close on each platform. It also leaves the required local macOS runtime observations unspecified (docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:117; docs/decisions/0065-ci-platform-evidence.md:18; plans/active/FORGE-WARM-1-hybrid-mode-reuses-warm-codex-worker-threads.md:238).
contradictions: The plan requires the SDK and external codex binary to have the same exact release, while the confirmed spec requires checking the binary against the SDK's minimum compatible version. A newer compatible binary would pass the spec but fall back under the plan; this change in route behavior has no disposition (docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:44; plans/active/FORGE-WARM-1-hybrid-mode-reuses-warm-codex-worker-threads.md:158).

The plan admits direct Claude task writers but its documentation list omits the confirmed strict-role-split spec, which still says Claude orchestrator product writes remain denied and fix rounds relaunch the plugin companion. Shipping the listed docs alone would leave a confirmed user flow contradicting the new behavior (docs/specs/strict-role-split.md:27; docs/specs/strict-role-split.md:44; plans/active/FORGE-WARM-1-hybrid-mode-reuses-warm-codex-worker-threads.md:208).
resolutions: FORGE_EXECUTOR applies to Claude-coordinated sessions; Codex-coordinated sessions keep native execution and refuse any other executor setting.
The recorded Claude-writer entry is the stage's write proof at close preflight and stage finish in place of a companion launch.
SDK pinned exactly; the codex binary must meet the SDK minimum; doctor --fix installs the pinned SDK and, when needed, the minimum codex.
Windows uses the existing private-file DACL helper for the supervisor socket token.
A task with any existing companion launch is a plugin task (route stickiness covers pre-upgrade tasks).
A recorded forge delegate --abandon-turn marks an unreadable turn failed and the task continues on a fresh thread (bounded recovery).
A resolution is delivered once the turn carrying it has started (recorded); older signals without turn ids keep today's meaning.
Activation boundary: the route stays off until SDK-ADMISSION, which includes terminal-turn proof; LIVE-EVENTS adds streaming, reattach and steering.
End-to-end adds an older-template client with an active plugin task upgraded twice, the task finishing on the plugin.
Each parity cell checks setup, init/adopt/upgrade, a refused out-of-scope write, hook delivery and task close; one real task per mode observed locally on macOS.
Follow the confirmed spec: exact SDK pin, binary at or above the SDK minimum.
The strict-role-split spec is added to the docs to amend.

The proposed end-to-end fixture starts with forge init on the current template. It does not exercise upgrade of an older existing client, preservation of an active plugin task, or a repeated upgrade, which are explicit acceptance outcomes (plans/active/FORGE-WARM-1-hybrid-mode-reuses-warm-codex-worker-threads.md:240; docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:113).

The verification plan names mode and route cells but does not assign falsifiable checks for the confirmed matrix's setup, init/adopt/upgrade, scoped writes, hook delivery, and task close on each platform. The plan admits direct Claude task writers but its documentation list omits the confirmed strict-role-split spec, which still says Claude orchestrator product writes remain denied and fix rounds relaunch the plugin companion. findings: The executor setting is independent of FORGE_COORDINATOR, but the plan does not route Claude execution when Codex coordinates or Codex execution when Claude coordinates in codex mode. Its verification labels codex mode as native Codex, leaving those combinations unproved (docs/decisions/0085-executor-modes.md:20; plans/active/FORGE-WARM-1-hybrid-mode-reuses-warm-codex-worker-threads.md:238).

Recording Claude sessions in a writer list does not identify what replaces the existing successful-launch requirement at both task-close preflight and stage finish. Claude-only work would still be refused without a plugin launch or degraded window (factory/scripts/forge_cli/stages.py:1831; factory/scripts/forge_cli/stages.py:4362).

The plan pins an external codex binary but specifies only SDK installation through doctor --fix. Today's repair installs @openai/codex@latest, so the proposed exact-version check has no stated way to install or repair its required binary (factory/scripts/forge_cli/doctor.py:1825; factory/scripts/forge_cli/doctor.py:1841).

The supervisor's owner-only socket and 0600 token specify POSIX permissions without a Windows ownership and ACL rule, despite native Windows parity being required. Existing private-file handling uses a separate Windows DACL check for this boundary (plans/active/FORGE-WARM-1-hybrid-mode-reuses-warm-codex-worker-threads.md:173; factory/scripts/forge_cli/delegate.py:1312).

Route stickiness begins at a task's first new-route delegation, but an in-flight pre-upgrade plugin task has no route field to consult. The plan does not say how its existing companion launch rows are recognized before choosing the SDK route (plans/active/FORGE-WARM-1-hybrid-mode-reuses-warm-codex-worker-threads.md:170; factory/scripts/forge_cli/delegate.py:784; docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:81).

An unknown turn blocks close until thread/read reports a terminal state, but the plan gives no recovery when the app-server dies before publishing one or the thread can no longer be read. That leaves a task permanently unable to close despite the repository's bounded-recovery requirement (plans/active/FORGE-WARM-1-hybrid-mode-reuses-warm-codex-worker-threads.md:193; docs/QUALITY.md:121).

Signal resolution currently becomes resolved immediately, with no task-turn identity or delivery acknowledgement. The plan does not define when a resolution counts as delivered, or how existing plugin and historical signals without turn IDs remain valid after the proposed schema change (factory/scripts/forge_cli/signal.py:219; factory/scripts/forge_cli/signal.py:231; factory/schemas/signal.json:6).
